claims.statement: Fan and Sun, Amending the Lonely Runner Spectrum Conjecture, arXiv:2306.10417 v2 (EJC 33(1) (2026) P1.38): Conjecture 1.3 (ML = s/(ns+k) with k <= n, or ML >= 1/n), Conjecture 6.1 (k <= n/2), Table 1 (their search: 7 speeds up to 70 with k in {1,2}; 8 speeds up to 60 with k = 1; no published counts or tuples; code unpublished).

Cordella, Odd denominators in the Lonely Runner spectrum for six speeds, arXiv:2609.03444 v2: near-tight definition (S2.1), Lemma 2.2 (witness times m/(v_i - e v_j), e = +-1), searches 7 speeds <= 50, 8 <= 40, 6 <= 110, Theorem 5.3 (v_max < 3q on the U_C family); code survey.c v1.0.2 (MIT, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22345079).
Lonely runner conjecture proved for at most 8 runners (classical for <= 7, Rosenfeld arXiv:2509.14111 for 8); Hu-Jing arXiv:2610.23790 (uniform gap) is not about the spectrum.

Equivalence and completeness. (a) With ML = p/q lowest terms and k' = q - np, Fan-Sun Conj 1.3 is exactly 1 <= k' <= n (k = g k'); Conj 6.1 is k' <= n/2. (b) For positive speeds the sum times m/(v_i+v_j), 1 <= m <= (v_i+v_j)/2, suffice: at a maximiser one active runner rises on the left and one falls on the right; if they differ t0 is a sum time, if equal then f(t0) = 1/2 and t0 is a sum time with m = D/2. Cordella's Lemma 2.2 uses sums and differences.

Scope: distinct speeds suffice (a repeated speed leaves at most n-1 <= 7 distinct speeds, and ML >= 1/n by the lonely runner conjecture for at most 8 runners); primitive tuples suffice (ML invariant under a common factor).

Null boxes: exhaustive enumeration with exact integer witnesses and Fraction-recomputed ML for every reported tuple gives primitive near-tight counts 7<=80: 37 (k1:33,k2:4); 8<=60: 36 (k1:36); 7<=200: 55 (k1:51,k2:4); 8<=130: 65 (k1:65); 6<=200: 1085 (k1:971,k3:114); controls 4<=200: 4125, 6<=110: 348, 7<=50: 29, 8<=40: 29 (other boxes in summary.json). No tuple has k > n or k > n/2. 7<=70 and 8<=60 recompute Fan-Sun Table 1; new relative to the literature are only 7 speeds in (70,200] and 8 speeds in (60,130], as null boxes. Conj 1.3 is neither proved nor refuted.

Independent AI audit: a Rust screen with the complete witness set (every reduced a/b <= 1/2, b <= 2N; sums, differences, peaks) reproduces every tuple set with p, q, k identically on all boxes including 8<=130 and 7<=200 (prefilter mode matched full mode on four boxes); Cordella's survey.c (reviewed, then run) matches the controls for 4<=200, 6<=110, 7<=50, 8<=40 and finds (2,7,9,11,13,20,54) ML 9/65 at 7<=56. Fraction check of all rows of 7<=80, 8<=60 and 40 random rows of 7<=200, 8<=130, 6<=200: 0 mismatches. NOT a human audit; producer N2/N3 and the float-grid check not re-implemented.

The four k=2 septuples (1,2,3,4,5,7,18), (1,3,4,5,7,13,18) ML 3/23, (1,3,4,5,7,11,30) ML 5/37, (2,7,9,11,13,20,54) ML 9/65 are re-verified exactly over the complete set; they are the same four in every box from <= 54 to 200. (2,7,9,11,13,20,54) is printed in neither paper, lies outside Cordella's 7-speed box (54 > 50), is found by his survey.c at 7<=56, and lies inside Fan-Sun's searched range (<= 70): NOT a new finding. That Fan-Sun saw it is an inference (their code is unpublished).

Secondary, descriptive: all 1085 sextuples <= 200 have ML = (P-1)/(6P), P = +-1 mod 6, with odd q; max v_max/q = 195/73 at (6,61,67,128,189,195) (a member of a family for which Cordella's Thm 5.3 already proves v_max < 3q: no new evidence); 13/5 at (1,4,5,6,7,11,39) for 7 speeds and 21/17 at (1,5,6,7,8,11,13,21) for 8 speeds.

NOT done: Lean or any proof-assistant check; the box 8<=150 (about 26,000 core-s, skipped by choice); the producer's W9 run on 8<=130 and 7<=200 (superseded by the auditor's complete screen); re-implementation of producer controls N2, N3 and the float-grid check; any search outside the boxes; a human audit. Recorded so the absences are explicit.
